cohort: 236 randomly selected non-pregnant females of reproductive age within a tea estate community in Hantana, Kandy district, Sri Lanka.
finding: The prevalence of anaemia was 33.1%, and it was significantly associated with being employed, delivery of a baby within the past 4 years, advancing age, low income (less than 20,000 LKR), and prolonged menstrual bleeding for more than 3 days.
